title: This Shrimp Punches So Hard It Breaks Aquarium Glass

scenes.text: There's a shrimp that punches hard enough to smash aquarium glass.
It's the peacock mantis shrimp, about the length of your hand, with two clubs folded under its face.
Those clubs fly out at over 80 kilometres an hour. The whole punch takes less than a thousandth of a second.
It accelerates like a bullet leaving a gun. Scientists needed cameras shooting thousands of frames a second just to see it.
It's so fast the water can't keep up. A bubble rips open behind the club and collapses with a bang, hitting the prey twice.
The power comes from a spring in its arm. It locks the club, loads it like a crossbow, and lets go. Would you keep one as a pet?

description:
There's a shrimp that punches hard enough to smash aquarium glass.
The peacock mantis shrimp strikes with its club-like appendages at 14 to 23 metres per second, with accelerations comparable to a bullet, as measured by researchers at UC Berkeley in 2004 using high-speed cameras. The strike is so fast it creates cavitation bubbles in the water that collapse and hit the prey a second time. A saddle-shaped spring in the arm stores the energy and releases it in a flash.
Would you keep one as a pet?
